originalTitle: The Tariff Cost: analysis of the costs to Americans from new tariffs on Canada
content:
It’s in your car, your soda cans, your window frames.

In 2025 the government put a tax on aluminum coming into the country. First 25 percent, then 50 percent. The reason given was to get America making more of its own. Aluminum got hit harder than almost anything else, so it’s a fair place to ask whether it worked.

A year and a half later, here’s what the government’s own figures show.

Now the part most people miss. The tax is only charged on metal from abroad. But when foreign metal costs more, American metal goes up to match, because nothing stops it. Same higher price, no tax paid.

To be fair: one company announced it’s restarting part of an idled plant, and a smelter takes years to build. This is also one metal, not the whole economy. But it’s the metal the tax was aimed at hardest, and this is what happened.

There is a fourth thing at stake, and it is not a tax: the energy Canada sells the U.S. That one is further down, under The nuclear option .

Customs writes down the tax on every shipment as it crosses the border. This is those records, added up.

Modelled estimate — not measured duty

Everything above is money customs really collected, and only on Canadian goods. This number is different. It is an estimate, and it is bigger, because it counts tariffs on all imports since 2025 — China, Mexico, Europe, Canada, all of them. It also rests on one thing no data can measure. When a company pays a tariff, some of that cost goes on the price tag and some of it does not. How much? Nobody knows for sure. The number we use, and where it came from, is in Method below.

Pick a state to see what the tariffs and the energy trade mean there.

Canada’s tax hits American exports — the things American workers grow and build. Right now the list is steel and almost nothing else. In September it adds food. Everything on the list is taxed 25% today. September brings in a 50% rate and moves hundreds of American steel and aluminum products up to it.

Canada has not done this, and nothing here says it will. But next to this, tariffs are small. Flip the switch to see which states buy their energy from Canada, and whether they have anywhere else to buy it.

— of energy the United States bought from Canada in six months

Every American product on Canada's list, all — of them. Filter it, or search for something specific.

These numbers are public. Almost nobody has seen them. If you know someone who should, send them the link.

Almost every number on this page was counted, not guessed. Nothing here is a prediction. There are two exceptions. The first is What tariffs cost your household , which needs a guess about price tags that no data can give us. The second is the money paid on American-made aluminum in Start with aluminum , which we worked out from a measured price and a measured tonnage instead of counting it directly. Both are labelled everywhere they show up, and both are explained in full below. Anywhere else, if the only way to answer a question was to guess, we say so and leave the number out.

Six public datasets, all free, all citable:

Two taxes, two sets of people paying. Canada’s tax is paid by Canadian importers, and it shows up in Canadian prices. What it does on this side of the border is hurt American exporters — the people who make what is on the list. Washington’s tax on Canadian goods is paid at the American border by American importers. That is the money counted in What you have already paid . Two different taxes, two different payers. Do not add them together.

What this page does not tell you , because the data cannot:

Counting lines on the list tells you how wide it is, not how much money is on it. One line can carry a billion dollars of trade, or almost none. That is why the dollar figures come from trade data instead of from the list.

Everything in Start with aluminum is counted except one figure: the money paid on American-made metal, which no customs record contains. What follows is printed by the code that did the work, so this text cannot drift away from what actually ran.

The one modelled number: what tariffs cost your household

The section itself says what this covers and what the one guess is. Below is the full list, printed by the code that did the work, so this text cannot drift away from what actually ran.
